'''''Ar nosurge: Ode to an Unborn Star'''''{{efn|Full name {{Nihongo|''Surge Concerto: Ar nosurge ~A Song that Prays for a Planet Being Born~''|アルノサージュ ～生まれいずる星へ祈る詩～|Arunosaaju ~Umareizuru Hoshi e Inoru Uta~}}}} is a Japanese [[role-playing video game]] developed by [[Gust Co. Ltd.|Gust]] and published by [[Koei Tecmo]]. Directed by Akira Tsuchiya, the game takes the anime art style of Gust's flagship ''[[Atelier (video game series)|Atelier]]'' video game series and puts it into a [[science fiction]] [[space opera]]-type setting. While playing as an RPG, the game is very story heavy, with virtually all gameplay mechanics feeding into the overall plot, including many segments playing as an interactive [[visual novel]]. Designed with player immersion as a core concept, the player actually plays as themselves, using their [[video game console]] as a means to communicate with characters as themselves, while otherwise controlling characters as one typically does in a video game. The game alternates between following two sets of characters - Delta and Casty, and Earthes and Ion, as they work through issues related to the hostile race known as Sharl that are antagonizing the space station that humanity currently lives on, while working through many of their own personal issues of their past.

The game debuted with a worldwide release on the [[PlayStation 3]] across in 2014. An extended version containing all of the game's [[downloadable content]] (DLC), ''Ar nosurge Plus'', was released worldwide the following year on the [[PlayStation Vita]]. A remastered high definition version, ''Ar nosurge DX'', was released in Japan in March 2021 for the [[Nintendo Switch]], [[PlayStation 4]] and [[Microsoft Windows]].

==Gameplay==
The game plays as a [[JRPG]] with [[visual novel]] segments.<ref name="HCGRev"/> On the role-playing side, the game does not have a [[party (role-playing games)|traditional party setup]],<ref name="RPGOutline">{{Cite web|url=https://www.rpgfan.com/review/ar-nosurge-plus-ode-to-an-unborn-star/|title=Ar nosurge Plus: Ode to an Unborn Star |website=www.rpgfan.com|date=2015-07-31 |first1=Andrew|last1=Barker|access-date=2021-02-26}}</ref> but rather, the game alternates between two sets of characters; Delta and Cass on one side, and Ion and Earthes on the other.<ref name="HCGRev"/> In the regular game field, the game plays as most JRPGs do; the player maneuver's the character through the game environment, exploring small areas to find [[non-player character]]s to interact with or items to collect to aid them through progressing the game.<ref name="EurogamerPrev">{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurogamer.it/articles/2014-09-24-ar-nosurge-ode-to-an-unborn-star-sette-dimensioni-per-un-jrpg-recensione-review|title=Ar nosurge: Ode to an Unborn Star, sette dimensioni per un jRPG - review|first=Emiliano|last=Baglioni|website=Eurogamer.it |date=September 24, 2014|language=it|access-date=2021-02-26}}</ref> In certain areas, a bar is present in the corner of the screen.<ref name="RPGamerRev"/> The bar indicates that [[random battle]]s may occur in that area, and indicate how increasingly likely they are to occur as movement transpires on the map.<ref name="RPGamerRev"/><ref name="RPGsiteVita"/> Optional [[small talk]] between characters arises as the game world is explored as well.<ref name="DDINT1"/>

The game employs a [[turn based]] battle system with timed button press elements that amplify effectiveness. Only two characters participate in a battle at the time - Delta or Earthes as the attacker/defender, and Cass or Ion who stands back to charge their "Song Magic" special move.<ref name="RPGamerRev">{{Cite web|first1=Sam|last1=Marchello|url=https://archive.rpgamer.com/games/arnosurge/arnosurge/reviews/arnosurgestrev1.html|title=RPGamer > Review > Ar Nosurge: Ode to an Unborn Star|website=archive.rpgamer.com}}</ref>  Multiple waves of enemies approach the player, which the player takes on each wave one at a time as each is defeated, with each wave placing characters on a 3x3 grid.<ref name="RPGOutline"/><ref name="RevolutionBattle"/> The player has a selection of different types of regular attacks, with varying strengths, weaknesses, and [[area of effect]]s, as well as the option of using consumable items or special "Friend Skills" earned through game progression that award various effects.<ref name="RPGOutline"/><ref name="2014DD">{{Cite web|url=http://www.digitallydownloaded.net/2014/10/review-ar-nosurge-ode-to-unborn-star.html|title=Review: Ar nosurge: Ode to an Unborn Star (Sony Playstation 3)|date=3 October 2014 }}</ref> The better the player strings together attacks, the faster the Song Magic's meter grows, which increases its attack power.<ref name="RPGOutline"/> Attacks phases can be extended if enemies are hit with a "break" status incurred by good fighting, though attack number are finite, and once they are used up, the attack phase ends.<ref name="RevolutionBattle">{{Cite web|url=https://www.gamerevolution.com/review/65687-ar-nosurge-ode-to-an-unborn-star-review|title=Ar Nosurge: Ode to an Unborn Star Review|website=GameRevolution|access-date=2021-02-26|date=2014-10-14|first1=Kevin|last1=Schaller}}</ref><ref name="RPGOutline"/> The battle transitions to the enemy phase, where the player must defends through time button presses to reduce damage aimed at Cass or Ion.<ref name="EurogamerPrev"/> Battles continue until one of four scenarios occur - the player defeats all enemies, the enemies deplete all [[health points]] of the Cass or Ion, both sides run out of turns, or if the player chooses to use the Song Magic attack.<ref name="2014DD"/> The more the Song Magic is charged, the more powerful it is, and the more it works towards eliminating random battles from the area.<ref name="EurogamerPrev"/> If the Song Magic meter is maxed out, the battle is automatically won, and random battles are eliminated from the area for the duration of the time spent there.<ref name="RPGOutline"/><ref name="RevolutionBattle"/><ref name="EurogamerPrev"/>

The rest of the game's gameplay modes more closely resemble a visual novel, largely revolving around reading text and choosing from [[dialogue tree]]s or other text-based options.<ref name="RPGamerRev"/><ref name="2014DD"/> The "Genometrics" segments are story segments where the player dives into a character's subconscious dream world to help them through various mental hang-ups they're suffering through in the game.<ref name="2014DD"/><ref name="RPGamerRev"/><ref name=gem0929/> The segments are split into 10-20 points on a map to be selected; each one revealing more of the narrative. Selecting each one costs Dive Points (DP), which are earned through participating in the game's battle system.<ref name="RPGamerRev"/> Certain dialogue options cost DP as well, and may hinder or help progression. If the player cannot pay the given cost of DP required, progress is halted, and the player returns to the main game. The segment is completed once enough DP is spent to read all text to the story's conclusion, and completion rewards the player with new "Song Magic" to be used in the game's battle system.<ref name="RPGamerRev"/><ref name="RPGsiteVita">{{Cite web|url=https://www.rpgsite.net/review/4432-ar-nosurge-plus-ode-to-an-unborn-star-review|title = Ar nosurge Plus: Ode to an Unborn Star Review &#124; RPG Site}}</ref><ref name="CubRev"/> The game's "Purification" segments involve two characters meditating and reflecting together on various events that had transpired in the main game.<ref name="RPGamerRev"/> The player is also given the option to equip "Genometrica Crystals" that are obtained through progression of the Genometrics segments, which give stat boosts for the game's battle system.<ref name="RPGamerRev"/> The game also contains an item synthesis system similar to the ''[[Atelier (video game franchise)|Atelier]]'' video game series.<ref name=gem0929/> Upon traveling to item shops, and talking to their respective shop keeper synthesis recipes are obtained.<ref name="CubRev"/> If the player has obtained the required items through game progression, they may combine them into new items.<ref name="CubRev"/> Each item creation contains a story scene about the respective item, and can be used in further synthesizing, or for added effects in battle.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2014/07/02/ar-nosurge-ode-to-an-unborn-star-coming-to-north-america|title=Ar Nosurge: Ode to an Unborn Star Coming to North America - IGN|date=2 July 2014|via=www.ign.com}}</ref><ref name="DDINT1"/>

==Synopsis==
===Setting and characters===
The bulk of the game takes place on a massive [[space station]] traveling through space.<ref name="2014DD"/> Humanity has been traveling through space on it for the last 5,000 years following the destruction of their home planet, Ra Ciela, which was destroyed by its own sun.<ref name="2014DD"/> Morale is generally low for its inhabitants – they long to live on in nature again, the ship is running out of resources, and they've been unable to find a new planet to sustain them.<ref name="2014DD"/> Additionally, they're under attack by a fairy-like race of humanoids called Sharls, who, with their innocent appearances and power of "Song Magic", lure people away to abduct them.<ref name="2014DD"/> Humanity is generally powerless against them, and must resort to sectioning off parts of the space station and hiding, and their numbers diminish.<ref name=gem0929/> However, after thousands of years have passed, the impassable "Fellion Wall" falls, and in are people called "ancients" - people essentially [[cryogenically frozen]] from the era when humanity still lived on Ra Ciela.<ref name=gem0929/> It appears human from this era once also possessed the ability to create "Song Magic", and thus, these people allow for the ability to fight back against the Sharl.<ref name=gem0929>2013-09-29, [http://gematsu.com/2013/09/ar-no-surge-first-details-screenshots Ar no Surge first details and screenshots], Gematsu</ref> Alternatively, there's another cult-like faction of people who believe in giving up and disappearing away with the Sharl, complicating matters.<ref name="RPGsiteVita"/>

The game follows the events of two separate pairs of main characters.<ref name="GameInformer1"/> Delta, an elite fighter from the organization of PLASMA, travels with his childhood friend Cass, who has the ability to wield song magic.<ref name="GameInformer1">{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.gameinformer.com/games/ar_nosurge_ode_to_an_unborn_star/b/ps3/archive/2014/07/01/sci-fi-jrpg-ar-nosurge-ode-to-an-unborn-star-coming-to-playstation-3.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140708051437/http://www.gameinformer.com/games/ar_nosurge_ode_to_an_unborn_star/b/ps3/archive/2014/07/01/sci-fi-jrpg-ar-nosurge-ode-to-an-unborn-star-coming-to-playstation-3.aspx|url-status=live|archive-date=July 8, 2014|title=Sci-Fi JRPG Ar Nosurge: Ode To An Unborn Star Coming To PlayStation 3|first=Kyle|last=Hilliard|magazine=Game Informer}}</ref> Both are Ancients from the city of Felion. The other pair is Ion, also able to wield rare Song Magic, and Earthes, a humanoid robot of unknown origins. Earthes is similar to a [[silent protagonist]] in the game: he is a vessel of which the player is supposed to be communicating directly into the game world, with game characters directly addressing the player, [[breaking the fourth wall]]. Other prominent characters include Nay, a friend of the four who holds a leadership role called the "Divine Empress", Kanon, a rival-turned-friend of Ion's past, Zill a church [[bishop]] who advocates working with the Sharl, Sarly a scientist friend of Delta and Cass, and Shirotaka, an [[otaku]] [[computer hacker]] friend of the groups.<ref name=4gamer>{{cite web |date=2013-11-05 |url=http://www.4gamer.net/games/234/G023461/20131030055/ |language=ja |title=「アルノサージュ ～生まれいずる星へ祈る詩～」，"詩魔法"がカギを握るバトルシステムや登場ヒロイン「キャスティ」「イオン」を紹介 |work=4gamer |access-date=2021-02-26 |trans-title=Introducing "Ar Nosurge-Poetry to pray for the born star-", the battle system where "poetry magic" is the key, and the heroines "Castie" and "Aeon" |archive-date=2013-11-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131105165109/http://www.4gamer.net/games/234/G023461/20131030055/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Development==
''Ar Nosurge'' was first announced in September 2013, as part of developer [[Gust Co. Ltd.|Gust]]'s 20th anniversary plans.<ref name=gem0924>{{cite web|date=2013-09-24 |url=http://gematsu.com/2013/09/ar-no-surge-announced-for-playstation-3 |title=Ar no Surge announced for PlayStation 3 |work=Gematsu|first1=Sal|last1=Romano|access-date=2021-02-26}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.siliconera.com/gust-celebrates-20th-anniversary-new-atelier-rorona-ar-nosurge/|title=Gust Celebrates 20th Anniversary With New Atelier Rorona And Ar NoSurge|date=November 9, 2013}}</ref> The game was directed by Akira Tsuchiya, who had previously directed Gust's ''[[Ar Tonelico]]'' trilogy of video games, and ''[[Ciel Nosurge]]''.<ref name=gem0929/> The games, along with ''Ar Nosurge'', are all part of Gust's extended "Exa Pico" fictional universe. The events of the ''Ar Tonelico'' trilogy connect to each other, but largely just occur in the same fictional universe rather than directly overlapping into ''Ar Nosurge''.<ref name="AiraTsuchiya"/><ref name="DDINT1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.digitallydownloaded.net/2014/07/interview-mind-behind-ar-nosurge-part-1.html|title=Interview: The mind behind Ar nosurge (Part 1)|first=Matt|last=S|access-date=2021-02-22|archive-date=2020-02-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200219144427/http://www.digitallydownloaded.net/2014/07/interview-mind-behind-ar-nosurge-part-1.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> ''Ciel Nosurge'', however, is considered a prequel  to ''Ar Nosurge'', and contains many common characters and settings, with the two often referred to collectively as the ''Surge Concerto'' duology.<ref name="AiraTsuchiya"/><ref name="DDINT1"/> Despite this, Tsuchiya created ''Ar Nosurge'' to be an entirely self-contained story that requires no knowledge of the other game's to understand the game's story.<ref name="AiraTsuchiya">{{cite web|url=https://www.otakustudy.com/video-game/2014/09/ar-nosurge-interview-akira-tsuchiya-director-surge-concerto-series/ |title=A Conversation with Akira Tsuchiya|date=2014-09-23|access-date=2021-02-26|website=otakustudy.com}}</ref> The game was meant to mix the anime style of Gust's other main franchise, ''[[Atelier (video game series)|Atelier]]'', while added a more in-depth [[science fiction]] story element to it.<ref name="DDINT1"/> The game's key concept was to create a game world that felt like an "actual existing world", where the player is playing a role in the story as themselves, using the [[video game console]] to communicate as themselves to the characters in the game.<ref name="DDINT1"/> Exploring realistic and in-depth bonds between characters was a main focus for the development team as well.<ref>{{cite magazine|date=2013-11-06 |url=http://www.famitsu.com/news/201311/06042788.html |title=『アルノサージュ』イメージムービーが初公開された"ガスト創立20周年発表会"をリポート！ 岸田メルさんや加隈亜衣さんも出演]|magazine=[[Famitsu]]|language=ja |trans-title=Report on "Gust 20th Anniversary Presentation" where the "Arnosage" image movie was released for the first time! Mel Kishida and Ai Kakuma also appeared |access-date=2021-02-26}}</ref> Some story events, such as the "Purification Ceremony" scenes, feature sexual overtones and innuendo; Tsuchiya implemented this to create more realistic interactions and relationships between characters.<ref name="DDINT1"/>  The game's battle system was developed to be flashy in presentation to hold the player's attention, but simple and quick in execution, as to keep the focus on the story and characters.<ref name="DDINT1"/> All aspects of the gameplay were built to feed into the game's story, in order to create a better sense of immersion.<ref name="DDINT2">{{Cite web|url=http://www.digitallydownloaded.net/2014/07/interview-mind-behind-ar-nosurge-part-2.html|title=Interview: The mind behind Ar nosurge (Part 2)|first=Matt|last=S|access-date=2021-02-23|archive-date=2021-02-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210213071511/http://www.digitallydownloaded.net/2014/07/interview-mind-behind-ar-nosurge-part-2.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Not all ideas related to creating a sense of immersion were included in the final game; at one point, the game contained enemy characters in battles that could "notice" the presence of the player, and would try to do things to "harm" the player, such as deleting their save game information.<ref>{{cite magazine|date=2014-05-05 |url=http://www.famitsu.com/news/201405/05052798.html |title=『シャリーのアトリエ』、『シェルノサージュ』の新情報も飛び出した！ 加隈亜衣さん出演"ガストトークショー"リポート【マチ★アソビ Vol.12】|language=ja|magazine=[[Famitsu]] |trans-title=New information on "Charlie's Atelier" and "Ciel Nosurge" has also popped up! Report on "Gust Talk Show" starring Ai Kakuma [Machi Asobi Vol.12]}}</ref> However, this was deemed too detrimental to the enjoyment of the game, and was removed prior any of the game's releases.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://killscreen.com/previously/articles/jrpg-monsters-eat-your-save-file-best-idea-and-worst-idea/|title=JRPG monsters that eat your save file are the best idea and worst idea|first=Jason|last=Johnson|date=May 7, 2014|website=Kill Screen|access-date=2021-02-26}}</ref>

===Release and versions===
''Ar Nosurge'' first released on the [[PlayStation 3]] in Japan on March 6, 2014, slightly delayed from its initial January 2014 release date.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2014-01-20/ar-no-surge-rpg-teaser-movie-posted | title=Ar no Surge RPG's Teaser Movie Posted | publisher=[[Anime News Network]] | date=January 20, 2014 | access-date=January 20, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.crunchyroll.com/anime-news/2014/01/21/video-gust-teases-ar-no-surge-rpg-with-new-clip-and-screens | title=VIDEO: Gust Teases "Ar no Surge" RPG with New Clip and Screens | publisher=[[Crunchyroll]] | date=January 22, 2014 | access-date=January 22, 2020}}</ref> The PS3 version was announced for an English localization shortly afterwards. While the game was commonly spelled ''Ar No Surge'' prior to localization, its final English title would be ''Ar Nosurge: Ode to an Unborn Star''.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.gematsu.com/2014/01/12-minutes-ar-surge-gameplay | title=12 minutes of Ar no Surge gameplay  | publisher=Gematsu | date=January 25, 2014 | access-date=January 25, 2020}}</ref><ref name="GemUSPS3"/> It was released in North America on September 23, 2014, and in Europe on September 26, 2014.<ref name="GemUSPS3">2014-06-25, [http://gematsu.com/2014/06/ar-nosurge-coming-europe-september-26 Ar nosurge coming to Europe on September 26], Gematsu</ref><ref>2014-07-01, [http://www.siliconera.com/2014/07/01/ar-nosurge-will-released-north-america-september-23rd/ Ar Nosurge Will Be Released In North America On September 23rd], Siliconera</ref> North American publisher [[NIS America]] released a limited edition on their online store that included a copy of the game, the soundtrack, a hardcover art book, and a poster.<ref name="Joystick1West">{{cite web|url=http://www.joystiq.com/2014/07/13/ar-nosurge-gets-limited-edition-gamestop-pre-order-incentives/|title=Ar nosurge gets limited edition, GameStop pre-order incentives|author=Thomas Schulenberg|work=Engadget|access-date=2014-09-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140922064058/http://www.joystiq.com/2014/07/13/ar-nosurge-gets-limited-edition-gamestop-pre-order-incentives|archive-date=2014-09-22|url-status=dead}}</ref> Some retailers bundled some of the game's [[Downloadable content]] (DLC) as a pre-order bonus as well.<ref name="Joystick1West"/> A number of sets of DLC was released for the PlayStation 3 version, including additional sets of "Purification" scene scenarios for the characters Kanon and Nay,<ref name="Joystick1West"/> two new "Genometrics" scenarios for the character Shirotaka, and some cosmetic character costumes. The game's soundtrack and two mini-albums with all of the game's vocal tracks released in the same month,<ref>{{cite web|date=2014-03-10 |url=http://www.4gamer.net/games/234/G023461/20140310055/ |title=「アルノサージュ」の音楽CD3作品がオリコンデイリーランキングにランクイン |work=4gamer |language=ja|access-date=2021-02-26|trans-title=3 music CDs of "Arnosage" ranked in the Oricon Daily Ranking}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|date=2014-03-10 |url=http://www.famitsu.com/news/201403/10049584.html |title=『アルノサージュ ～生まれいずる星へ祈る詩～』関連CDが、オリコンCDアルバムデイリーランキング2位・3位・5位にランクイン |magazine=[[Famitsu]] |access-date=2021-02-26|trans-title=CDs related to "Ar Nosurge-Pray for the Born Stars-" are ranked 2nd, 3rd, and 5th in the Oricon CD album daily ranking]}}</ref> while a prequel [[manga]] was released in promotion of the game the month prior in ''[[Monthly Shōnen Sirius]]''.<ref>{{cite web |date=2014-02-26 |url=http://www.4gamer.net/games/234/G023461/20140226080/ |title=「アルノサージュ」の漫画がニコニコ静画「水曜日のシリウス」で26日より連載開始 |language=ja |trans-title=The manga of "Arnosage" will be serialized on Nico Nico Seiga "Sirius on Wednesday" from the 26th. |work=4gamer |access-date=2021-02-26 |archive-date=2019-04-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190403215931/https://www.4gamer.net/games/234/G023461/20140226080/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

An enhanced port of the game, '''''Ar Nosurge Plus''''' was released for the [[PlayStation Vita]] shortly after. This release contained all of the original's DLC, additional cosmetic character costumes, and a new expanded tutorial.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://gematsu.com/2014/06/ar-nosurge-plus-debut-screenshots |title=Ar nosurge Plus debut screenshots |website=Gematsu|date=2014-06-29|access-date=2021-02-26|first1=Sal|last1=Romano}}</ref><ref name="RPGsiteVita"/> It was released on October 2, 2014, in Japan, {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714183315/http://gematsu.com/2014/06/ar-surge-plus-announced-ps-vita |date=2014-07-14 }}, Gematsu</ref><ref>{{cite Message and Events to Come|date = 20 March 2019}}</ref> Another enhanced release, '''''Ar Nosurge DX''''', was announced in 2020 for the [[Nintendo Switch]], [[PlayStation 4]], and [[Microsoft Windows]] platforms.<ref>{{cite web|date=2020-06-25|url=https://www.gematsu.com/2020/06/ciel-nosurge-dx-and-ar-nosurge-dx-announced|title=Ciel nosurge DX and Ar nosurge DX announced|work=Gematsu|access-date=2021-02-26|first1=Sal|last1=Romano|archive-date=2020-11-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201101143812/https://www.gematsu.com/2020/06/ciel-nosurge-dx-and-ar-nosurge-dx-announced|url-status=live}}</ref> delayed to March 4, 2021 in Japan|url=https://www.gematsu.com/2020/12/ciel-nosurge-dx-and-ar-nosurge-dx-delayed-to-march-4-2021-in-japan|website=Gematsu|date=December 21, 2020|access-date=December 21, ==Reception==
{{Video game reviews
| MC = PS3: 67/100<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.metacritic.com/game/ar-nosurge-ode-to-an-unborn-star/critic-reviews/?platform=playstation-3 |title=Ar nosurge: Ode to an Unborn Star for PlayStation 3 Reviews |website=[[Metacritic]] |publisher=[[Red Ventures]] |access-date=2022-02-27}}</ref><br />Vita: 77/100<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.metacritic.com/game/ar-nosurge-ode-to-an-unborn-star/critic-reviews/?platform=playstation-vita |title=Ar nosurge Plus: Ode to an Unborn Star for PlayStation Vita Reviews |website=[[Metacritic]] |publisher=[[Red Ventures]] |access-date=2022-02-27}}</ref>
}}

The game was generally well received by critics. Critics generally praised the game's story, albeit with the notion that it could be confusing and overwhelming at first.<ref name="HCGRev"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://rpgamer.com/review/ar-nosurge-plus-ode-to-an-unborn-star-review/|title=Ar nosurge Plus: Ode to an Unborn Star Review|date=6 July 2015 }}</ref><ref name="RPGsiteVita"/><ref name="CubRev">{{Cite web|url=http://www.cubed3.com/review/2152/1/ar-nosurge-plus-ode-to-an-unborn-star-ps-vita.html|title = Ar nosurge Plus: Ode to an Unborn Star (PS Vita) Review - Page 1 - Cubed3 | date=2 April 2018 }}</ref> ''Hardcore Gamer'' praised the game's emphasis on story over common JRPG concepts like [[grinding (video games)|grinding]], stating that although the story and scope may be overwhelming at first, that "once the stories start to intertwine, and a few startling revelations come to light, the script doesn't seem quite as bonkers. Characters you'll grow to love change alongside your own, and a multitude of communicative sources...make it easy to become invested...while it doesn't break the glass ceiling of video game narrative design, it certainly leaves its hand prints across the stretch."<ref name="HCGRev">{{cite web|url=http://www.hardcoregamer.com/2014/10/06/review-ar-nosurge-ode-to-an-unborn-star/108132/|title=Review: Ar Nosurge: Ode to an Unborn Star|work=hardcoregamer.com|date=6 October 2014 }}</ref> Similarly, ''RPGSite'' said that the ''Plus'' version of the game "remains one of the better modern entries in the genre. Players will uncover some brilliant character relationships and outstanding music that will remain with you long after the credits have rolled."<ref name="RPGsiteVita"/> ''[[Famitsu]]'' gave the game a review score of 32/40.<ref>2014-02-25, [http://gematsu.com/2014/02/famitsu-review-scores-issue-1317 Famitsu Review Scores: Issue 1317], Gematsu</ref>

The PlayStation 3 version of ''Ar nosurge'' sold 27,037 physical retail copies within the first week of release in Japan, placing fifth within the Japanese software sales rankings for that particular week.<ref>2014-03-12, [http://gematsu.com/2014/03/media-create-sales-3314-3914 Media Create Sales: 3/3/14 – 3/9/14] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170728124913/http://gematsu.com/2014/03/media-create-sales-3314-3914 |date=2017-07-28 }}, Gematsu</ref> The Vita release of the ''Plus'' version sold another 9,240 units at retail in Japan later in the year as well, placing ninth for the week.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gematsu.com/2014/10/media-create-sales-92914-10514|title = Media Create Sales: 9/29/14 – 10/5/14|date = 8 October 2014}}</ref> While no exact Western sales figures were released, Sony revealed that ''Plus'' was the eighth most downloaded game for the Vita in North America in its release month of July 2015, which encompasses all sales of the title, as it did not receive a physical retail release outside of Japan.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://blog.playstation.com/2015/08/07/playstation-store-july-2015s-top-sellers/|title=PlayStation Store: July 2015's Top Sellers|date=7 August 2015|access-date=2 March 2021|archive-date=25 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210125115230/https://blog.playstation.com/2015/08/07/playstation-store-july-2015s-top-sellers/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==See also==
*''[[Chronos Materia]]'' - a new [[intellectual property|IP]] proposed by Gust in 2013 that would have shared elements of the ''Ar Nosurge'' and ''Atelier'' series that was cancelled in 2016
*''[[Baten Kaitos: Eternal Wings and the Lost Ocean|Baten Kaitos]]'' - a 2004 [[JRPG]] by [[Monolith Soft]] that shared a similar [[fourth wall]] breaking premise of the player having a direct role in the game
